title: Chiral quantum chaos around exponentially many zero modes in the quantum breakdown model
authors: Kohei Kawabata, Kinya Guan, Hosho Katsura
abstract: The quantum breakdown model is a model of randomly interacting fermions, motivated by the physics of dielectric breakdown. Here, we establish classification of symmetry and quantum chaos in a zero-dimensional, all-to-all-interacting version of the quantum breakdown model. It exhibits the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ periodicity with respect to the number of fermionic modes, reminiscent of the symmetry classification of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model. A unique feature of the quantum breakdown model is that it realizes all the five classes with chiral symmetry and hosts an exponentially large number of many-body zero modes protected by the chiral index. We elucidate the separation and scaling of the spectral gap and demonstrate the symmetry-enriched hard-edge spectral statistics as signatures of quantum chaos in the chiral symmetry classes.
summary: This work investigates the quantum breakdown model, a random fermion model, to classify its symmetries and quantum chaotic behavior. It finds that the model exhibits $\mathbb{Z}_4$ periodicity and possesses an exponentially large number of zero modes protected by chiral symmetry. The findings provide signatures of quantum chaos through characteristic spectral statistics near the energy origin.
main_problem: The paper establishes a classification of symmetry and quantum chaos in the quantum breakdown model, focusing on the spectral statistics.
main_result: The model exhibits $\mathbb{Z}_4$ periodicity and realizes all five chiral symmetry classes, hosting an exponentially large number of zero modes protected by the chiral index.
method: The analysis involves systematic classification of symmetries and quantum chaotic spectral statistics using exact diagonalization and comparison to random matrix theories.
model_or_system: The system is the quantum breakdown model, a model of randomly interacting fermions motivated by dielectric breakdown, analyzed in a zero-dimensional, all-to-all-interacting version.
key_observables: Spectral statistics (bulk and hard-edge), spectral gap separation, and the number of many-body zero modes.
important_parameters: The number of fermionic modes ($N$), and the chiral index ($\nu$).
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the random all-to-all interacting version in a zero-dimensional setting.
figures_summary: Figures show the density of states for varying N, illustrating the separation of zero modes from the bulk spectrum, and comparisons to Wigner-Dyson distributions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the Hamiltonian, classifies symmetries based on $N \pmod 4$, and then examines spectral properties, including the zero-mode count and the hard-edge spectral statistics.
why_interesting: The study of spectral statistics and symmetry protection in a highly interacting, random model provides insights into non-trivial quantum phases, analogous to those studied in disordered or strongly correlated systems.
